- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, particularly after recent spikes in history.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — overestimates after high values and underestimates after low values.
- Forecasts lag behind true values by 1–3 days, especially in the first 10 days of the forecast.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum after sharp price drops; underestimates falling trends.
- Overconfidence in short-term spikes leads to overforecasting in the 1–5 day horizon.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — fails to adjust quickly to new data, especially when true values deviate from recent history.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–7 days, then gradually converge toward true values — suggesting a delayed correction mechanism.
